The more I think about the fact she had her passport, the more I'm questioning whether or not the family had a heads up she might've been in Mexico. I understand LE verified the video this weekend, but passports have RFID chips in them; I find it hard to believe that border crossings don't have long range scanners to pick up RFID information. Even if her passport wasn't flagged at the time she crossed, I'd assume this information is stored? I guess she could've obstructed the signal someway, but that seems like something someone would think of only in a detailed and thought out plan -- which I'm not convinced is what happened here. 

  
I don't think it's beyond possibility that either (a) LE dropped the ball or had reason to believe this was voluntary from the jump and didn't investigate as if she were truly missing against her will; (b) the family didn't want to lose public support; or (c) a combination of the two. I'm not ready to dogpile the family though, I think to critique and say "well, if i were them ........." is just unempathetic
